discovery: Proposal and realization of electron-spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots

nominees.name: David P. DiVincenzo
nominees.affiliation: RWTH Aachen University and Forschungszentrum Jülich, Germany

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech, Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

motivation: In 1998 Loss and DiVincenzo proposed using the spin of a single electron confined in a gate-defined semiconductor quantum dot as a qubit, with exchange coupling between neighbouring dots providing two-qubit gates. This turned the mesoscopic quantum dot, until then a playground for transport and quantum chaos, into a platform for coherent quantum control. Vandersypen and colleagues led the experimental realization: single-shot spin readout, driven coherent rotations of a single electron spin, and later high-fidelity one- and two-qubit gates and multi-qubit processors in isotopically purified silicon. The field has since established spin-bath decoherence physics, spin-charge hybridization and scalable CMOS-compatible architectures. Coming after the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits, this would recognize the complementary, microscopic route: individual electron spins in solids, engineered atom by artificial atom into controllable quantum matter.
